I used Teracopy on Windows and I liked it because it has a few options on top of the built-in copy dialog. Now that I'm on Fedora Linux I'm looking for a utility that has this feature specifically: the ability to copy a directory full of files and only overwrite existing files when the existing files are older than what's available with the same name (basically the equivalent of running CP with the -u tag, except with a GUI and more importantly, a progress bar).

My use case is that I keep a hard drive full of media that I keep backed up to an external hard drive, both of them NTFS. Normally I'd just need to copy the whole directory to the external drive and choose "skip existing", except that sometimes I make corrections to media and I need those corrections to replace the existing where appropriate. For example, I might have media that requires subtitles and doesn't have them, so I realize the mistake and correct the file. "skip all existing" won't replace the faulty file with the correction, and "replace all existing" means adding unnecessary time/work to the copy job because it's replacing a whole bunch of identical files. What I need is to be able to copy all files, and skip existing unless the new file is newer than the existing file, in which case replace it.

Is there anything that has this functionality outside of the terminal "cp -u" command?

pv allows a user to see the progress of data through a pipeline, by giving information such as time elapsed, percentage completed (with progress bar), current throughput rate, total data transferred, and ETA.
